newsitem.title: USA: U.S. said willing to consider more aid to N.Korea.
newsitem.headline: U.S. said willing to consider more aid to N.Korea.

text.p: The United States said on Thursday it would consider providing additional food aid to North Korea on humanitarian grounds but declined to tie aid directly to a deal for Korean peninsula peace talks.

"The United States ... has no plans at this time to provide additional food aid to North Korea. We continue to monitor the situation closely. We will consider future appeals for food aid. But ... we contribute food aid based on humanitarian needs," State Department spokesman John Dinger told reporters.

"We have from the beginning provided the food aid and humanitarian assistance ... based on humanitarian needs, not linked to political developments. And that is how we intend to continue," Dinger said.

He was responding to comments by South Korean officials in Seoul who reported that impoverished North Korea had agreed to join proposed four-nation peace talks if the United States and South Korea first guaranteed food aid.

Dinger confirmed the United States, South Korea and North Korea held a working level meeting in New York on Wednesday on a U.S.-South Korean proposal for negotiations on a permanent peace for the Korean peninsula that would also include China.

But he insisted: "No agreement of any sort was reached at yesterday's meeting. We understand (North Korea) is still considering our proposal ... And we hope the DPRK will agree soon to four-party talks."
